title: Embedded Software Manager, Mobile Robotics
descriptionHtml:
Come lead the embedded software team behind the world's largest fleet of mobile robots — and behind the next generation of them. Your team's software runs on more than a million robots working around the clock in Amazon fulfillment centers across North America, Europe, Japan, and Australia. These drive units are the backbone of the fulfillment engine: most Amazon orders pass through them, and they are a key enabler of one-day and same-day Prime delivery.

This role has two halves and both are hard. One is systematic reliability at scale: any single robot can fail without anything breaking, but the system as a whole has to keep moving, and a firmware change ships to the entire world — so the bar is not whether one robot works, it's whether a change is safe across a million of them. The other is a new robot on a demanding schedule, where the hardware, the software, and the requirements are all being invented at once.

Your team owns the software that makes each robot move and keeps it safe — real-time motion control, power and charging, connectivity, and the safety components that hold a robot in a safe state — across every generation in the fleet and the new robots still being designed. You won't write most of the code, but you'll own the decisions, and you'll pick up the ball yourself when nobody else does.

Key job responsibilities
As the manager of this team, you will:
- Hire and develop world-class embedded software engineers into effective teams, solving challenges that have never been solved before
- Draw on your own experience to review, guide, and coach the team, helping them avoid pitfalls and produce products and systems that are world-class and industry-leading
- Own your team's software and the data it produces: keep credibility as a technical peer, lead the response when something goes wrong in the field, make fleet behavior measurable, and prove a change is safe across the whole fleet before it ships worldwide
- Use operational and product metrics to decide what to fix, what to build, and what to stop doing
- Organize the team's work so priorities, commitments, and progress are visible to the team and its partners; forecast dates you can defend, and re-plan when the fleet or the program moves them
- Balance technical leadership and business judgment on long-term technology decisions, and represent the team in business planning, technical estimation, and the written documents that set direction

A day in the life
No two days look the same. You might start one-on-one with a couple of engineers, working through how they're doing and what they need to grow. Later you're writing up your team's long-term strategy without dropping the short-term commitments. After lunch you sit down to re-plan the next two weeks, because a hardware change just moved what's possible. Then your team pulls you into a deep dive: something's happening at one site, on a handful of robots out of the thousands there, and nobody yet knows if it's software, hardware, or the first sign of something bigger. They want tactical leadership, and you don't disappoint — you get them the data and a plan, and they spring into action. You close the day finding a way to recognize the people who made it great.

About the team
We are a group of super-smart, collaborative doers who keep the world's largest robot fleet moving and build the robots that will join it. We work shoulder to shoulder with the mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing engineers who build those robots, and with the operations teams who live with what we ship. We take our responsibility for safety seriously, but challenge ourselves to produce the right product that also gives us the performance we need. We pay attention to the details so others don't have to, and we let the data tell us where to look next.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of engineering team management experience
- 3+ years of providing technical leadership and project management for all aspects of the software development lifecycle experience
- 5+ years of Software Engineer, Software Developer, or related occupational experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Knowledge of engineering practices and patterns for the full software/hardware/networks development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, certification, and livesite operations
- Experience partnering with product or program management teams
- Experience leading the development of embedded, real-time, or safety-critical systems

Preferred qualifications

- Experience delivering products against plan in a fast-paced, multi-disciplined, distributed-responsibility and often ambiguous environment
- Experience in recruiting, hiring, mentoring/coaching and managing teams of Software Engineers to improve their skills, and make them more effective, product software engineers
- Experience in tools for custom embedded Linux distribution creation such as Yocto, and familiarity in developing and debugging Linux kernel
- Experience sustaining a large fleet of deployed devices, including over-the-air firmware update, telemetry, and remote diagnostics at scale
- Experience at the boundary between embedded devices and cloud services (device connectivity, fleet management, or IoT platforms)
- Familiar developing in a safety standards controlled environment such as IEC 61508 or ISO 26262

• Data center support projects
• Special initiatives and innovation projects

You will drive significant cost reductions by minimizing change orders, eliminating scope gaps between contractors, reducing construction schedule delays, optimizing vendor pricing, and decreasing project management and engineering labor costs through standardization and clear documentation.

The ideal candidate brings a comprehensive knowledge in data center environmental controls systems, IT infrastructure, networking, mechanical facility operations, electrical power monitoring, and project management, combined with strong leadership and collaboration skills.

If you are passionate about customer experience, think and act with a global perspective, and want to contribute to sophisticated innovations in building controls and automation for the world's largest cloud infrastructure, we want to hear from you.

Key Job Responsibilities:

• Develop and maintain deep expertise in building operations, mechanical plant strategies, BMS/EPMS programming concepts, control diagrams, industrial HVAC systems, electrical lineups, one-line diagrams, and complex environmental and electrical concepts

• Anticipate roadblocks and risks while providing escalation management and resolution
• Travel globally as needed to manage and support project initiatives

• Collect feedback data and lessons learned to arrive at unified, documented solutions
• Support risk identification and mitigation efforts during site assessments and project lifecycle phases

Our Controls Design Engineers:
• Are controls subject matter experts (SMEs) with their knowledge of building operations, electrical generation and distribution equipment (i.e. generators, UPS etc.), mechanical plant and strategies (i.e. AHUs, chillers etc.), BMS/EPMS programming concepts, control diagrams, industrial HVAC, electrical line-ups, one-line diagrams, and complex environmental and electrical concepts

descriptionHtml:

Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. title: Principal Manufacturing Test Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking a Principal Manufacturing Test Engineer to define and drive the test strategy across a product line scaling from prototype builds toward high-volume manufacturing. This is a senior technical leadership role — you'll own the test architecture from concept through volume, set the standards and frameworks that guide the broader test and manufacturing engineering team, and build the organizational capability to execute complex test operations at scale. You sit at the seam between validation and production — creating clarity on what gets tested, how, and why, and ensuring the test infrastructure evolves in lockstep with the product and the production system.

The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of experience designing, deploying, and scaling manufacturing test systems for complex electromechanical products — including hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, in-line functional test, and parametric data collection. You should have a track record of standing up test operations from scratch, driving multi-generational test strategy across product iterations, and influencing product architecture decisions to improve testability. This role demands strategic thinking, deep technical credibility, and the ability to align cross-functional teams — engineering, validation, software, manufacturing, and quality — around a unified test philosophy that scales.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and own the end-to-end manufacturing test strategy — what gets tested, where (in-line vs. EoL vs. sampling), and how — across build iterations from prototype through volume production. Set the multi-generational test roadmap and investment plan.

- Serve as the test voice in design trades — influence product architecture, interface design, and tolerance strategy to improve testability. Drive design-for-test (DFT) considerations upstream as a co-designer, not just a reviewer.

- Create clarity from ambiguity: establish test frameworks, standards, and decision criteria that guide the broader engineering team. Define what "ready to test" means at each build stage and own the test readiness process as part of manufacturing readiness.

- Partner with Engineering, Validation, and Quality leadership to align V&V requirements with production test capability. Translate validation intent into a production test philosophy that balances thoroughness, cycle time, and cost at scale.

- Architect the test data strategy — define schemas, traceability frameworks, pass/fail logic, and export standards designed for direct dashboard ingestion (Grafana, QuickSight, or similar). Ensure test data enables real-time production visibility, trend analysis, and closed-loop design feedback without post-processing.

- Drive the design and deployment of manufacturing test systems — electromechanical subassembly test stations, HIL rigs, in-line functional/parametric test, and end-of-line acceptance test — sized for medium-to-high throughput and architected for operator execution at rate.

- Design operator-friendly test setups that inform high-volume line requirements — intuitive UIs, clear pass/fail indicators, guided error recovery, and work instructions that enable L1 operators to execute complex test sequences reliably. Engineer the test flow to balance throughput with learning.

- Specify and procure test instrumentation — DAQ hardware, sensors, power supplies, electronic loads, motion controllers, communication interfaces (CAN, EtherCAT, SPI, UART) — making strategic build-vs-buy decisions on test hardware, fixtures, and platforms.

- Scale test solutions from single-station, engineering-attended toward multi-station, operator-run, and fully instrumented — designing modular, replicable test cells that can be deployed across lines and sites.

- Analyze test data to drive quality and design improvements at a systems level — identify trends, correlate failures to root cause, and feed actionable insights back to design, process, and quality engineering. Own the feedback loop between the test floor and the next design iteration.

- Raise the bar on hiring, develop the team's test engineering capabilities, and mentor engineers. Shape the test engineering culture — technical rigor, data discipline, and operational excellence.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Manufacturing Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline.

- 10+ years of manufacturing test engineering experience for electromechanical or robotic products, including experience spanning both NPI/prototype and high-volume production environments.

- Experience owning manufacturing test strategy for a new product introduction (NPI) from concept through volume production.

- Hands-on experience developing and deploying in-line and end-of-line functional test systems, including test sequence creation, pass/fail criteria definition, and parametric/SPC data collection.

- Proficiency in test software/frameworks (e.g., LabVIEW, NI TestStand, Python-based test automation or custom solutions) and DAQ/instrumentation specification.

- Demonstrated experience architecting test data pipelines for dashboarding and analytics — structured data formats, schemas, and traceability frameworks designed for consumption, not just storage.

- Demonstrated ability to create clarity from ambiguity — defining test strategy, frameworks, and decision criteria for cross-functional teams.

- Ability to influence at a senior level across engineering, validation, quality, and manufacturing leadership.

- Proven ability to implement test systems end-to-end — fixture build, instrumentation integration, and on-floor debug. Technical support available; hands-on execution is not optional.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) test system design and deployment at production scale

- Experience standing up test operations for a greenfield or brownfield manufacturing facility

- Experience in robotics or complex electromechanical manufacturing test
- Experience with high-throughput test cell design (cycle time optimization, parallel test, multi-station architectures)

- Familiarity with data visualization tools (Grafana, QuickSight, etc.) and structured data formats (JSON, Parquet, SQL databases)

- Experience with communication protocols common in robotic/electromechanical systems (CAN, EtherCAT, SPI, UART, Ethernet/IP)

- Experience scaling test systems from prototype quantities to volume production (100+ units/day)

- Knowledge of GD&T, measurement system analysis (MSA/Gage R&R), and statistical process control

- Master's degree in a relevant engineering discipline

descriptionHtml:

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep. You'll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You'll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day. Here, the impact of what you build isn't abstract, it's visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world's most complex operations moving forward. This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

This is not a corporate, remote or office-based position. This is a full-time, early career position located within one of Amazon’s fulfillment centers, sort centers, delivery stations or other operations buildings. Amazon is seeking customer focused individuals to lead a team of hourly employees across our Operations network! Our warehouses are fast-paced environments where standing, walking, and having on-the-production floor conversations are common as a supply chain leader.

As an Area Manager, you will be responsible for engaging, leading and developing your team in a warehouse environment. Your main focus will be motivating, mentoring, and managing your team to meet goals. Amazon provides extensive training and development to become an exceptional people leader. As a people manager, you will ensure that your team has all the tools needed to succeed and maintain the highest levels of safety, quality, attendance and performance at work.

• Work independently and operate in an autonomous environment.
• Stand/walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours.

A day in the life
As an Area Manager, no two days look exactly the same, but every shift gives you the chance to lead a team, solve real problems, and directly impact how millions of customers receive their orders.
Start of Shift: Set the Tone
• Get a handoff from the outgoing manager and review what's carrying over so nothing falls through the cracks.
• Lead a team huddle to kick off the shift. Huddles are used to align on goals, safety priorities, and key focus areas.
• Confirm your team is in place, positioned for success, and ready to go before operations begin.
Middle of Shift: Lead from the Floor
• Walk the floor regularly to stay connected to your team, spot issues early, and keep things running smoothly.
• Drive results across safety, quality, and productivity — balancing all three in real time.
• Adjust staffing and resources as volume and priorities shift throughout the day.
• Coach and develop your team members, respond to challenges as they come up, and partner with support teams to remove roadblocks.

End of Shift: Close Strong
• Do a final walkthrough to make sure your area is clean, organized, and set up for the next team's success.
• Review your shift's performance data and capture what went well and what to improve
• Hand off to the incoming manager with a clear picture of priorities, open items, and next steps.
• Wrap up any remaining administrative tasks so you leave the shift with a clean slate.
• Every shift, you'll see the direct results of your leadership: from the energy of your team to the packages that reach customers' doorsteps. This is where your decisions have real, visible impact.

You are the person on the floor who turns capacity plans into operational reality.

As an Rack Lifecycle Tech, you will execute structured cabling, rack installation, and decommission activities with precision and to standard — following established SOPs, escalating deviations to your team lead, and ensuring every rack you touch is installed correctly, cabled to specification, fully documented, and handed off with zero blockers, prepare SOP’s with new processes, stake holder management with cross functional teams. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities.


Key job responsibilities
🔷 Rack Installation & Cabling
· Execute rack installations including physical placement, power connections, grounding, and cable management per AWS standards and MOPs
· Perform structured cabling including fiber/copper terminations, patch panel connections, labeling, and dressing to specification
· Complete OTDR and power testing; validate results against acceptance thresholds; escalate failures to team lead promptly rather than self-resolving outside approved procedures
· Follow all EHS protocols, lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and safe work practices during installation activities
🔷 Rack Lifecycle Operations
· Execute work orders and tasks assigned by the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager under direct manager direction, maintaining accurate status updates in workflow management tools (e.g., Boost, MARS)
· Perform quality checks on completed cabling work including port map verification, label accuracy, and as-built documentation updates in CMDB/DCIM
· Identify and escalate issues, blockers, or deviations from SOPs encountered during task execution to the team lead or manager promptly; do not self-resolve outside approved procedures
· Support deployment wave readiness by participating in pre-work site walks, material staging, and tool preparation
🔷 Material Handling & Supply Chain Support
· Receive, verify, and stage incoming rack, cable, optics, and hardware deliveries; validate against BOM and flag discrepancies
· Maintain accurate site inventory records for cables, optics, patch cords, and consumables used during deployments
· Support cycle count activities and assist in identifying inventory shortfalls that may impact deployment timelines
🔷 Handover & Documentation
· Complete all required as-built documentation, port maps, test result records, and workflow sign-offs before handoff to Data Center Operations
· Update CMDB/DCIM and IPAM records accurately following rack installation or decommission activities
· Ensure handoffs are clean and fully documented with zero open blockers, enabling smooth transition to the next lifecycle phase
🔷 Rack Decommissioning
· Execute physical decommission activities per assigned MOPs — including cable removal, power disconnects, asset de-tagging, and rack extraction
· Perform device wipe and media destruction in compliance with AWS Secure Media Destruction and EHS policies
· Sort, label, and stage recovered assets (optics, cables, PDUs, hardware) for RMA, redeployment, or secure disposal per AWS Reverse Logistics policy
· Update DCIM/CMDB, IPAM, and port maps post-decom to ensure accurate space, power, and circuit records
· Validate that reclaimed U-space, power, and cooling capacity is accurately recorded in the available pool
🔷 Quality, Safety & Compliance
· Adhere to all site-level SOPs, quality standards, and governance frameworks for cabling, installation, and decommission activities
· Complete all required safety training and certifications; participate in regular EHS audits and team safety briefings
· Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying recurring quality issues, suggesting process improvements, and sharing feedback with the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager
· Use Rack Lifecycle Team tooling (e.g., Boost, MARS, ALM/DCLM) accurately to record work, track assets, and maintain data integrity
🔷 Cross-Team Coordination
· Support coordination with DCO, DCEO, Network Engineering, and facilities teams during active deployment or decom activities under manager guidance to ensure smooth execution
· Participate in daily stand-ups and pre-work briefings; communicate clearly on task status, blockers, and schedule adherence
· Provide accurate, timely updates on task completion and flag risks or delays to the team lead immediately
🔷 Continuous Learning & Development
· Maintain and develop technical proficiency in structured cabling, fiber optics, rack installation, and data center physical infrastructure
· Complete required certifications and training modules including EHS, LOTO, and any Rack Lifecycle Team-specific technical programs
· Proactively seek feedback from leads and managers to improve personal performance and output quality
· Support the onboarding and training of new team members; share knowledge and best practices with peers to build overall team capability and quality standards
· Stay current on AWS infrastructure tooling, cabling standards, and process updates communicated by the Rack Lifecycle Team


A day in the life
As a Rack Lifecycle Tech, your day is on the data center floor. You might start the morning by reviewing your assigned work orders in Boost, checking in with your team lead on priorities, and staging cables and optics for a rack installation wave. By midday, you could be terminating fiber runs at a patch panel, running OTDR tests to validate loss results against acceptance thresholds, or labeling and dressing a freshly installed rack. In the afternoon, you might be updating CMDB records for completed work orders, de-tagging and staging recovered assets from an EOL decom, or helping onboard a new technician by walking them through the SOP. If you encounter a deviation from the approved MOP, you escalate it to your team lead immediately — you don't improvise. Your role is hands-on, technical, and precise — you execute the work that keeps AWS capacity on track.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and Amazon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Senior Indirect Tax Analyst, International Indirect Tax Compliance
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's global indirect tax team in London and play a pivotal role in managing one of the most complex areas of Amazon's worldwide tax function, spanning EMEA, LATAM, and APAC. You'll work with AI-assisted tools, collaborate with senior tax leaders across multiple geographies, and directly shape how Amazon tracks and reports indirect tax reserves for hundreds of legal entities worldwide.

As a Tax Analyst on the ITX Compliance team, you will support the FAS5 quarterly close cycle, Amazon's central system for managing indirect tax loss contingencies under US GAAP (ASC 450). Your work will sit at the intersection of tax technical expertise and data-driven process management, where you'll review and challenge reserve positions, prepare VP-level reporting packs, coordinate with issue owners and directors across regions, and drive continuous improvement of critical reporting workflows. This is an opportunity to deepen your expertise in contingency accounting while contributing to a high-visibility programm that is actively investing in automation and innovation.

Key job responsibilities
1. Support the quarterly FAS5 close cycle for indirect tax contingencies across EMEA, LATAM & APAC including data validation, issue owner coordination, and multi-regional reporting;
2. Review and challenge indirect tax reserve and watch-list positions for alignment with US GAAP (ASC 450) recognition thresholds, and ensure FAS5 templates are compliant at each quarter-end and year-end reporting cycle;
3. Assist prepare director- and VP-level reporting packs with variance analysis, portfolio movement summaries, and data quality checks;
4. Coordinate with issue owners and Central VAT Accounting teams to resolve data completeness gaps and classification issues;
5. Maintain and continuously improve FAS5 portal workflows, including access management, and use Excel, the FAS5 portal, and AI-assisted tools to automate recurring reporting tasks;
6. Monitor changes in indirect tax legislation across covered jurisdictions and assess the impact on existing reserve positions and watch-list items;
7. Develop and maintain robust documentation supporting reserve positions, including technical memorandum, exposure analyses, and supporting schedules;
8. Liaise with internal stakeholders (accounting, legal, tax planning) and address audit queries related to the FAS5 process, providing clear and well-organised responses;
9. Support broader ITX Financial Health activities, including VAT balance sheet reconciliation, ageing analysis, and compliance systems management.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Knowledge of strong understanding of tax compliance principles, regulations, and reporting requirements across jurisdictions
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office products and applications at an advanced level
- Experience working in a large public accounting firm or multi-national corporate tax department
- Experience in tax with an EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa) focus
- Experience a compliance focused tax role in a multinational and/or professional organization

Preferred qualifications

- Experience researching indirect tax issues including taxability of products and services
- Knowledge of at least one data-focused technology tool, such as Python, SQL, Alteryx, Amazon QuickSight, or similar
- professional tax, accounting or legal qualification (e.g., Chartered Accountant (CA), Associate Chartered Accountant (ACA), Chartered Tax Adviser (CTA), Chartered Institute of Taxation (CIOT) or similar)

title: Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.
NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Physical Requirements:
• Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
• Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
• Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection
This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility
Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.


Key job responsibilities
• Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
• Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
• Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
• Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
• Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
• Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
• Role may support more than one location/site.


A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of electrical or mechanical, or 1+ years of data center or mission critical facilities (example: hospital, military facility, public safety facility, etc.) experience
- 1+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible shifts including night shifts/weekends

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Associate's degree in related field, or technical degree in related field
- Technical (Military/Trade School) training

title: Vehicle Design Engineer, Prime Air Vehicle Design & Test
descriptionHtml:

You’ll be responsible for designing conceptual level vehicle configurations and layouts that integrate all subsystems and meet vehicle level requirements. You'll model internal subsystems, major structural elements, and the OML of the vehicle. Your designs will feed into our suite of multi-disciplinary optimization (MDO) tools to help size the vehicle and mature the design. You’ll explore new and novel drone vehicle conceptual designs in both focused and wide open design spaces, with the ultimate goal of meeting our customer requirements. You’ll have the opportunity to prototype vehicle designs and support wind tunnel and other testing of vehicle designs. You will directly support the Office of the Chief Program Engineer, and work closely across all vehicle subsystem teams to ensure integrated designs that meet performance, reliability, operability, manufacturing, and cost requirements.

How do you get items to customers quickly, cost-effectively, and—most importantly—safely, in less than an hour? And how do you do it in a way that can scale? Our teams of hundreds of scientists, engineers, aerospace professionals, and futurists have been working hard to do just that! We are delivering to customers, and are excited for what’s to come. Check out more information about Prime Air on the About Amazon blog (https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/transportation/amazon-prime-air-delivery-drone-reveal-photos).

Our Flight Sciences Vehicle Design & Test organization includes teams that span the following disciplines: Aerodynamics, Performance, Stability & Control, Configuration & Spatial Integration, Loads, Structures, Mass Properties, Multi-disciplinary Optimization (MDO), Wind Tunnel Testing, Noise Testing, Flight Test Instrumentation, and Rapid Prototyping.

- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent
- 5+ years of experience in air or space vehicle configuration design and integration
- Vehicle level design intuition and ability to operate & analyze at the system-of-systems level
- Proficient in CATIA/3DX
- Proficient in surfacing/lofting

Preferred qualifications

title: Principal Technical Product Manager, Prime Video Commerce Personalization and Member Experience
descriptionHtml:
Come build the future of entertainment with us. Are you interested in shaping the future of movies and television? Do you want to define the next
generation of how and what Amazon customers are watching?

Prime Video is a premium streaming service that offers customers a vast collection of TV shows and
movies — all with the ease of finding what they love to watch in one place. We offer customers thousands of popular movies and TV shows from Originals and Exclusive content to exciting live sports events. We also offer our members the opportunity to subscribe to add-on channels which they can cancel at anytime and to rent or buy new release movies and TV box sets on the Prime Video Store. Prime Video is a fast-paced, growth business — available in over 240 countries and territories worldwide. The team works in a dynamic environment where innovating on behalf of our customers is at the heart of everything we do. If this sounds exciting to you, please read on.

Hundreds of millions of customers open Prime Video every week. They trust us to help them find something great to watch. Increasingly, they expect us to help them discover title offers, channel and bundle subscriptions that match their interests.

Today, we break that trust in small but compounding ways. A customer declines an offer and sees it again minutes later. A new subscriber gets upsells before finding a show they love. A loyal viewer showing signs of leaving receives a generic message that ignores everything they have ever watched.

We are hiring a Principal PMT to own Commerce Personalization for Prime Video. You will build the intelligence that makes every commerce interaction feel like it comes from a service that actually knows you.

This is a build-and-scale role. You will define what "right offer, right moment, right customer" means at Prime Video scale. You will ship systems that remember what customers have told us, respect their journey stage, and earn the right to make a recommendation. You will prove — through measurable customer outcomes — that respecting customer drives better business results than pressuring them.

Key job responsibilities
Own the customer problem end-to-end. Define the vision, strategy, and roadmap for Commerce Personalization across all Prime Video surfaces — homepage, detail pages, checkout, notifications, and partner storefronts.

Eliminate the contradictions customers experience today. Build coordinated intelligence, so a declined offer stays declined, at-risk customers get content before commerce, and new subscribers aren't treated like conversion targets. Define how we measure success and how it impacts our long-term success.

Crack problems others haven't, drive adoption at scale enabling Partner content discovery for the growing number of channels across 30+ countries. Personalized offer timing that converts because it's welcome

Ship fast, prove impact continuously. Start with the most painful customer contradiction and fix it. Every phase delivers measurable improvement — reduced repetition, better timing, higher engagement among at-risk segments. Build conviction through results.

Work backward from customers to technology. Partner with Applied Science and ML Engineering on reinforcement learning, multi-objective optimization, and unified customer representations — always in service of a specific customer outcome.

Drive organizational alignment. Get multiple teams to optimize shared customer outcomes over local metrics. Win this argument with evidence, not authority.

About the team
PV Commerce Personalization & Member Experience sits at the intersection of Prime Video's content experience and its commerce engine. We own the models, systems, and product experiences that determine which customers see which offers, when, and how. Our production models — including offer propensity, churn prediction, subscription ranking, and cross-offer optimization — serve decisions across every Prime Video commerce surface. We are evolving from siloed model optimization to a unified system that coordinates across the full customer journey. We are a product development team that partners closely with cross-functional teams across Prime Video to deliver customer and partner value.

Basic qualifications

- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience in technical product management, program management or engineering
- Experience owning feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience with end to end product delivery
- Experience leading engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience owning and delivering end-to-end product strategy for ML/AI-powered consumer products.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with subscription or commerce business models and LTV-based decision making.
- Familiarity with reinforcement learning, multi-armed bandits, or multi-objective optimization applied to product personalization.
- Track record of shipping products that changed customer behavior at scale (100M+ users).
- Experience with experimentation design, causal inference, and long-term holdout measurement.

title: Software Development Manager, S3 - Simple Storage Service
descriptionHtml:
Amazon S3 handles hundreds of millions of requests per second for customers around the world — and every one of those requests runs on software your team ships. As a Software Development Manager for S3 Foundations, you will own how new S3 software is built, validated, released, and observed across every AWS Region on the planet, at a scale almost no other engineering role can offer.

Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) provides industry-leading scalability, data availability, security, and performance for object storage. Customers of all sizes, from day-one startups to the world's largest enterprises, use Amazon S3 to deliver next-generation applications ranging from data analytics to AI to photo and video archives. While S3 has seen tremendous growth since launch in 2006, we are still in the early stages of realizing its full potential.

The S3 Foundations team is the foundation and force multiplier for S3's front-end engineering organization. We own the platform that safely delivers software to the fleet processing every S3 API request worldwide, from pre-production validation and qualification systems that catch problems before customers ever see them, to the post-processing services — metering, API events, and request logging — that power billing, auditing, and analytics for millions of AWS customers. When your team does its job well, customers get new S3 capabilities sooner.

This is a hands-on leadership role at the intersection of massive-scale distributed systems, developer experience, and operational excellence. You will:
- Own the roadmap for one of the highest-leverage platforms in S3 delivering front-end request processing.
- Drive an ambitious multi-year modernization agenda — increasing release frequency, compressing worldwide deployment times, hardening automated deployment safety, and re-architecting legacy services into modern, independently deployable systems.
- Build the self-service "builder experience" platform that lets S3 engineers validate, deploy, and observe their changes without waiting on anyone — measured by how much faster and safer they ship.
- Make AI a central pillar of how your team builds and operates: AI-assisted development as standard practice, spec-driven modernization of legacy services, automated on-call assistants, and create agents that handle routine requests.

Success in this role requires a leader who can move fluidly between weighing in on the engineering details of high-throughput distributed systems, prioritizing across a portfolio of platform programs, partnering with senior engineers and leaders across S3, and growing a team of talented builders. Because your platform is on the path of every S3 request worldwide, a passion and discipline around operational excellence, security, and availability is essential. Come build with us and make history with Amazon S3!

Key job responsibilities
- Lead, grow, and develop a team of software engineers, fostering a culture of technical excellence, deep ownership, and customer obsession.

title: Senior Product Manager - Technical, External Services, AWS Billing
descriptionHtml:
We're rebuilding the AWS product catalog for an AI-native world, and this role owns both how it's defined and how it grows. You'll set the standards every AWS product follows and define the new features, packages, and add-ons that service teams bring to customers, building the machine-readable foundation that billing, cost management, and AI agents all depend on. The AWS Billing organization serves over 200 AWS services across 30+ regions, and every one needs a product definition that is structurally correct, consistently described, and rich enough for both humans and AI to reason about. This is the foundation for commercial decisions made by external customers and internal teams.

As Senior Product Manager - Technical External Services, you'll own the AWS product model end to end: the schema, governance rules, and quality standards every product conforms to, and the new product structures service teams build on top of them. You'll define what attributes a product carries from creation, how to create standard models for different types of services (from compute and storage to AI inference and developer tools), how products relate to and compose with one another in packages and shared commercial experiences, and how the catalog enables AI agents to discover, compare, and act on products programmatically. You'll also extend the catalog with new product features, packages, and add-ons that service teams can adopt through configuration rather than custom engineering. Your work directly determines how AWS services launch and grow their products.

In this role, you'll architect the data model that underlies AWS commerce, define the governance framework that enforces it across hundreds of service teams, and establish the lifecycle and relationship standards that let products evolve and work consistently across commercial channels. You'll conduct direct research with service teams and internal consumers of product data to understand where definitions break down, translating those insights into schema improvements and governance rules. You'll work at the intersection of data architecture, billing infrastructure, and AI-native product design, defining how AWS products present themselves to the next generation of consumers.

You'll collaborate with engineering teams across AWS's billing, metering, and cost management organizations. This role requires deep technical fluency in data modeling, schema design, and systems thinking, combined with the product instinct to know which standards matter and which create bureaucracy.

If you're excited about defining the foundational data layer that makes AWS's commerce systems work this role offers the chance to shape how every AWS product is defined, described, and used across AWS commerce.

title: Shift Area Manager, Last Mile Operations
descriptionHtml:
When you join Amazon as an Area Shift Manager, you’ll gain experience leading a large and diverse team to make sure your area of the business keeps pace with demand. In this hands-on role, you’ll learn about the complexity of operations at a global business and what it takes to make everything run seamlessly. While you implement your team’s approach to drive productivity, you’ll also work closely with your colleagues to address challenges, which means no two days will be the same.
Amazon is looking for high-potential leaders, who are ready to own their impact in Amazon Operations as an entry-level manager working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. You will have your leadership capacity stretched to its full potential, As a front-line leader, you will have an opportunity to truly invest in others and develop a people-focused leadership style, while mastering the tools, processes, and operations that have created the most customer-centric company on Earth. If you want to be involved in continuing to define the future of online retail, and are dynamic and an organized self-starter, join our team in Amazon Operations.
Job Specifics:
- This role is fully onsite and requires flexibility to work and rotate shifts: weekends, holidays, and/or overnight shifts, and Ability to work overtime both in peak season and as needed.

Key job responsibilities
- Promote a culture of safety and wellbeing
- Analyze and implement corrective actions to make sure quality and productivity are at consistently high levels, and business objectives are met across all shifts
- Support and lead a team and handle administrative work alongside building and supporting a strong team culture
- Analyze performance and suggest process improvements to optimize work and improve customer service
- Promote best practice and continuous process improvements across your team in areas like health and safety and productivity
- Collaborate with other managers to standardize shift processes


A day in the life
You’ll work shifts and be based at one of our operational sites. Your main focus will be to maintain safety standards within your team and across your site. You’ll also monitor and maintain process efficiency. Your days will always include prioritizing routine team management and daily operational tasks, alongside other tasks like individual escalations, process improvement work and wide-scale operational contingency planning.

Being a key part of the operations team involves working with colleagues in other teams and external partners to make sure we stay on track to meet our customer demands and targets. This will involve analyzing data and performance metrics with leaders in your business area, as well as discussing the operational pros and cons of technical improvements with engineers.

About the team
Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- 2+ years of performance metrics, process improvement or lean techniques experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Knowledge of Microsoft Excel at an advanced level, including: pivot tables, macros, index/match, vlookup, VBA, data links, etc.

Preferred qualifications

- Speak, write, and read fluently in English

descriptionHtml:

You'll join a diverse team of hardware and network engineers, logistics specialists, security and safety experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You'll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you'll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We are looking for a detail-oriented, technically skilled Rack Lifecycle Tech to join our Rack Lifecycle Team within AWS Infrastructure Operations. In this individual contributor role, you will be a hands-on executor responsible for the physical installation, cabling, handoff, and decommissioning of racks across your assigned data center site. You are the person on the floor who turns capacity plans into operational reality.

As an Rack Lifecycle Tech, you will execute structured cabling, rack installation, and decommission activities with precision and to standard — following established SOPs, escalating deviations to your team lead, and ensuring every rack you touch is installed correctly, cabled to specification, fully documented, and handed off with zero blockers, prepare SOP’s with new processes, stake holder management with cross functional teams. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities.


Key job responsibilities
🔷 Rack Installation & Cabling
· Execute rack installations including physical placement, power connections, grounding, and cable management per AWS standards and MOPs
· Perform structured cabling including fiber/copper terminations, patch panel connections, labeling, and dressing to specification
· Complete OTDR and power testing; validate results against acceptance thresholds; escalate failures to team lead promptly rather than self-resolving outside approved procedures
· Follow all EHS protocols, lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and safe work practices during installation activities
🔷 Rack Lifecycle Operations
· Execute work orders and tasks assigned by the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager under direct manager direction, maintaining accurate status updates in workflow management tools (e.g., Boost, MARS)
· Perform quality checks on completed cabling work including port map verification, label accuracy, and as-built documentation updates in CMDB/DCIM
· Identify and escalate issues, blockers, or deviations from SOPs encountered during task execution to the team lead or manager promptly; do not self-resolve outside approved procedures
· Support deployment wave readiness by participating in pre-work site walks, material staging, and tool preparation
🔷 Material Handling & Supply Chain Support
· Receive, verify, and stage incoming rack, cable, optics, and hardware deliveries; validate against BOM and flag discrepancies
· Maintain accurate site inventory records for cables, optics, patch cords, and consumables used during deployments
· Support cycle count activities and assist in identifying inventory shortfalls that may impact deployment timelines
🔷 Handover & Documentation
· Complete all required as-built documentation, port maps, test result records, and workflow sign-offs before handoff to Data Center Operations
· Update CMDB/DCIM and IPAM records accurately following rack installation or decommission activities
· Ensure handoffs are clean and fully documented with zero open blockers, enabling smooth transition to the next lifecycle phase
🔷 Rack Decommissioning
· Execute physical decommission activities per assigned MOPs — including cable removal, power disconnects, asset de-tagging, and rack extraction
· Perform device wipe and media destruction in compliance with AWS Secure Media Destruction and EHS policies
· Sort, label, and stage recovered assets (optics, cables, PDUs, hardware) for RMA, redeployment, or secure disposal per AWS Reverse Logistics policy
· Update DCIM/CMDB, IPAM, and port maps post-decom to ensure accurate space, power, and circuit records
· Validate that reclaimed U-space, power, and cooling capacity is accurately recorded in the available pool
🔷 Quality, Safety & Compliance
· Adhere to all site-level SOPs, quality standards, and governance frameworks for cabling, installation, and decommission activities
· Complete all required safety training and certifications; participate in regular EHS audits and team safety briefings
· Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying recurring quality issues, suggesting process improvements, and sharing feedback with the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager
· Use Rack Lifecycle Team tooling (e.g., Boost, MARS, ALM/DCLM) accurately to record work, track assets, and maintain data integrity
🔷 Cross-Team Coordination
· Support coordination with DCO, DCEO, Network Engineering, and facilities teams during active deployment or decom activities under manager guidance to ensure smooth execution
· Participate in daily stand-ups and pre-work briefings; communicate clearly on task status, blockers, and schedule adherence
· Provide accurate, timely updates on task completion and flag risks or delays to the team lead immediately
🔷 Continuous Learning & Development
· Maintain and develop technical proficiency in structured cabling, fiber optics, rack installation, and data center physical infrastructure
· Complete required certifications and training modules including EHS, LOTO, and any Rack Lifecycle Team-specific technical programs
· Proactively seek feedback from leads and managers to improve personal performance and output quality
· Support the onboarding and training of new team members; share knowledge and best practices with peers to build overall team capability and quality standards
· Stay current on AWS infrastructure tooling, cabling standards, and process updates communicated by the Rack Lifecycle Team


A day in the life
As a Rack Lifecycle Tech, your day is on the data center floor. You might start the morning by reviewing your assigned work orders in Boost, checking in with your team lead on priorities, and staging cables and optics for a rack installation wave. By midday, you could be terminating fiber runs at a patch panel, running OTDR tests to validate loss results against acceptance thresholds, or labeling and dressing a freshly installed rack. In the afternoon, you might be updating CMDB records for completed work orders, de-tagging and staging recovered assets from an EOL decom, or helping onboard a new technician by walking them through the SOP. If you encounter a deviation from the approved MOP, you escalate it to your team lead immediately — you don't improvise. Your role is hands-on, technical, and precise — you execute the work that keeps AWS capacity on track.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and Amazon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field
- 2+ years of Computer Hardware Repair, Infrastructure Cabling, Network Deployment, Data Center Operations, or Technical Project Management experience
- 2+ years of network cabling, fiber optics, and test equipment including VFL, power meter, and OTDR experience
- 2+ years of fiber handling and fiber installation processes experience
- Can lift and rack equipment up to 40 pounds

Preferred qualifications

- Can work in cramped spaces or in elevated locations while adhering to health & safety guidelines

descriptionHtml:

title: Engineer Operations Technician , DCEO Operations Team
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

Technical writing to support change management program

Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

Key job responsibilities
● 日本におけるフロンティアモデルの共同GTMおよびパートナー戦略を策定・実行し、日本パートナープランを策定するとともに、AGS（AWSグローバルセールズ）日本リーダーシップが定める優先顧客需要シグナルに沿った日本戦略イニシアチブを定義する。
● AnthropicおよびOpenAIの国内アライアンスリードとのパートナーリレーションシップを担当し、日本カントリーレベルでの主要な窓口およびリレーションシップオーナーとして活動する。
● パイプラインの創出と共同販売モーションの実行を推進し、案件を選定からクローズまで進めるとともに、各案件のデリバリーおよびリセールにおけるパートナーのデリバリー準備を確保する。
● 日本カントリーレベルでの必勝アカウントおよびパイプラインレビューをリードし、AIスペシャリストやパートナーテクニカルリードと連携して案件のブロッカーを解除し、顧客の採用を加速する。
● 日本GSI/SI共同戦略を策定・実行し、パートナー主導のデリバリー能力を拡大し、パートナーエコシステムを多様化する。
● AWSフィールド内でビジネスチャンピオンを募集・育成し、フロンティアモデルの認知度向上と共同販売エンゲージメントを拡大する。
● EBC（エグゼクティブブリーフィングセンター）およびパートナー向けの顧客エンゲージメントをリードし、戦略的な案件を加速する。
● クロスファンクショナルチームを調整し、日本GTMの実行を管理する。AIスペシャリスト、AWSパートナーリーダーシップチーム、パートナーソリューションアーキテクト、アカウントマネージャー、パートナーセールズマネージャーと協力する。
● パートナー関連およびシステミックなブロッカーを48時間以内にAPJコアチームにエスカレーションし、案件が社内プロセスを待つことのないようにする。
● 主要指標を追跡・報告する：ARR、TCV、パイプラインカバレッジ、共同販売コンバージョン率、および日本レベルでのパートナープログラムの有効性。
● AWS Focus、ScaleおよびIndirectセールスチームに対し、フロンティアモデルのポジショニング、顧客選定基準、およびパートナーエンゲージメントモーションについてコーチングおよびイネーブルメントを行う。

A day in the life
一日は、ポートフォリオ全体をみたパイプラインデータの確認、案件の進捗状況のレビュー、ブロッカーの洗い出しから始まるかもしれません。午前中は、AIスペシャリストと協力して、主要なエンタープライズアカウントへの戦略的なGTMセールズプレイの展開に取り組みます。昼食後は、フロンティアパートナーとの共同販売機会の推進に関する通話があり、その後、AWSアカウントマネージャーグループに対して最新の共同販売プレイとパートナーバリュープロポジションのイネーブルメントを行います。午後は、セールス、ソリューションアーキテクチャ、マーケティングの点と点をつなぎ、案件を前進させます。一日の終わりには、フィールドから新しいビジネスチャンピオンを採用し、各アカウント全体でフロンティアモデルの認知度を高めることができる人材を見つけます。

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of developing, negotiating and executing business agreements experience
- 5+ years of Go-To-Market, Business Development, Sales, or Consulting experience
- 5+ years of working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage experience
- Experience developing strategies that influence leadership decisions at the organizational level
- Japanese Fluency and Business level English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience interpreting data and making business recommendations
- Experience identifying, negotiating, and executing complex legal agreements
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience selling enterprise software or cloud-based applications
- Experience explaining complex technical concepts to various business and technical audiences
- Experience presenting to both technical and non-technical executive audiences
- フロンティアAIモデルまたはプラットフォームパートナーシップの管理経験（例：Anthropic、OpenAI、または同様の基盤モデルプロバイダー）
- 共同販売モーションの実行およびパートナーチャネルを通じたパイプライン創出の実績
- GSI/SI共同戦略の策定・実行によるパートナー主導デリバリーの拡大実績
- オペレーティングモデル、ガバナンスメカニズム、および大規模なフィールドイネーブルメントの構築経験
- AI/MLインフラストラクチャのエコノミクスに対する理解（GPU容量、推論コスト、モデルデプロイメントアーキテクチャ）

title: Channel Team Lead, OTR, AMZL
descriptionHtml:
Amazonでは、地球上で最もお客様を大切にする企業であることを目指しています。これに向けてモチベーションにあふれ、実行力の高い人材を必要としております。

今回、Amazonは、我々の輸配送チームのチャネル・チーム・リード （CTL）を募集しています。Amazonは世界において最も知名度の高いブランドの１つであり、数百万点に及ぶ商品を大切なお客様に向けて絶え間なくお届けしています。
（※チャネルとは、お客様へお荷物を配送するための手段や経路を指しています）

【Amazon Hub デリバリーパートナープログラム概要】
Amazonからの業務委託を受けた一般小売店を代表とする独立事業主（法人）・個人事業主の皆様が、地域に根差したビジネスを展開されている強みを活かして近隣のお荷物を配送頂き、サイドビジネスとして収入を得て頂くAmazonラストマイルの新しいビジネスモデルです。
Amazon Hub デリバリー ホームページ：
https://logistics.amazon.co.jp/hubdelivery/marketing
Amazon Hub デリバリー パートナー様紹介動画：
https://m.media-amazon.com/images/G/09/DSP2022/hub/assets/fujii-shoten_1.mp4

【Job Summary】
このチャネル・チーム・リード （CTL）のポジションは、兵庫県エリアを中心に、Amazonと業務委託契約を締結する配送ストアの開拓、契約、及び配送オペレーションを推進し、配送ストアのパフォーマンス管理やオペレーション計画の実行をサポートします。

■このポジションで実現できること
・新規配送パートナー/ストアの開拓を通じて、Amazonの配送ネットワーク拡大に貢献
・新規配送パートナー/ストアとの協業を通じて、配送品質や顧客体験を改善
・オペレーションを直接支える役割として、目標に対しての改善や成果を実感できる
・多様な関係者との調整を通じて、営業・オペレーション双方のスキルを習得

【勤務地】兵庫県エリア

【パートナーシップマネジメント】
・新規配送パートナー/ストアの開拓および契約推進
・配送パートナー/ストアに対するAmazon配送モデルのトレーニングやコーチング
・配送パートナー/ストアの目標達成(配送量／配送品質)を実現
・配送パートナー/ストア訪問や派遣社員との連携を通じた信頼関係の構築

【オペレーション管理】
・配送パートナー/ストアの配送パフォーマンスをモニタリングし、定期的にレポート作成
・担当エリアにおける配送オペレーションから発生する日々のトラブル対応
・社内の関係部署と協業し、配送プロセスの改善を推進

【業務改善・効率化】
・パフォーマンス低下の原因分析と改善策の提案
・配送パートナー/ストアの契約継続率向上を目的とした施策の実行

======================================
関連情報
・所属部門:ラストマイル(AMZL)
・勤務地: 関西エリアDS
・オペレーション部門のDEIの取り組み
======================================

Basic qualifications

- 4年制大学卒、社会人経験２年以上
- ビジネスレベルの日本語力

Preferred qualifications

- 1年以上の物流、営業、コンサル経験など
- 周囲との円滑なコミュニケーションを通じて信頼関係を構築できる方

title: Sr. Seller Manager, Amazon Now
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about the rapidly evolving world of grocery Q-commerce? Do you want to be part of a high-energy team that is shaping the future of online grocery shopping? We are seeking a dynamic and forward-thinking Senior Seller Manager to join our pioneering team. In this pivotal role, you will serve as the dedicated owner of the instock function on behalf of sellers — ensuring seller inventory health, product availability, and supply chain efficiency across the platform.
As a Senior Seller Manager, you will be the strategic bridge between Amazon's operational capabilities and the sellers who depend on us to drive their instock performance. You will partner closely with sellers to diagnose root causes of instock gaps, implement scalable solutions, and build the processes that ensure sustained product availability for customers.
The ideal candidate thrives on ambiguity and excels at first-principle problem-solving. You are someone who can connect the dots across diverse workstreams, managing and influencing stakeholders at all levels to achieve breakthrough results.
A successful candidate will possess:
• Exceptional analytical skills and data-driven mindset
• Strong business acumen and strategic thinking capabilities
• Robust project management skills with a track record of delivering complex, cross-functional initiatives
• Outstanding communication and interpersonal skills to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders
• Unwavering customer obsession and relentless focus on delivering value
• High level of adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment

From selection optimization to sourcing strategies, network design, transshipment planning, demand forecasting, S&OP forecasting, in-stock management, and supply chain planning – you'll be orchestrating a symphony of workstreams that cut across functions, all aimed at ensuring optimal instock performance on behalf of sellers.
Join us on this exhilarating journey and be a catalyst for change in the world of grocery e-commerce.


Key job responsibilities
From selection optimization to sourcing strategies, network design, transshipment planning, demand forecasting, S&OP forecasting, in-stock management, and supply chain planning – you'll be orchestrating a symphony of workstreams that cut across functions.

Basic qualifications

- Experience and understanding of the retail and wholesale landscape in India and exposure to prior interactions with sellers and distributors
- Experience analyzing data and best practices to assess performance drivers
- Experience managing and growing complex business relationship at scale
- 6+ years of demand & supply planning experience

Preferred qualifications

- MBA
- Experience developing and executing sales strategies, tactics, plans, processes, systems, and programs.
- Experience managing and growing complex business relationship at scale
